releases.notes:
- First test of updates from inside the program
- No functional changes

- Packages for macOS now carry a fixed beta signature
- No functional changes

- Second package with the fixed beta signature, to test that macOS keeps its permissions after an update
- No functional changes

- Audio mixer has its own tab; the Audio Mixer button opens it
- Fixed: Outputs could appear below the mixer
- First package for Windows (screen capture works; window capture, camera, sound and recording are untested there)

- Input settings open as movable windows; several can be open at once
- Colour correction per input: wheels or bars for lift, gamma, gain and offset, basic levels, colour tables (LUT, .cube)
- Monitor in the colour page: picture, waveform, RGB parade, vectorscope
- Sound delay per input and at the output
- Transitions Wipe, Zoom and Slide
- Add input opens as a window; untested on Windows: camera, recording, capture of single windows

- Feedback button: report a bug or ask for a feature from inside the program, with a picture of what you mean
- Add input and the Media page are sorted by kind: Video, Image, Audio file, Convert, Camera, Screen, Audio input, Title, Colour
- Drag a tile to reorder the inputs, or drop it on the preview or program picture; drop files from the Explorer onto the window to add them
- Undo and redo (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y) for removing, moving, renaming and adding inputs
- Recording as MP4 or MOV (Settings, Recording); MP4 is the default on Windows
- Since beta.5 also: streaming, audio mixer with EQ, compressor and gate, stinger, cue lists, MultiView, several canvases, keyframes, lighting, tally, PTZ cameras and projectors – most of it not yet tested on real equipment

- Audio on several devices: master, the buses A to D, listening (solo) and timecode (LTC) can each play on a device of their own (Settings, Audio), with a delay per bus
- Audio mixer: faders with a dB scale up to +10 dB, the level meter (green, yellow, red) inside the fader, every channel a panel of its own; a yellow tag at the top tells you when no sound goes out
- New inputs: Stream (SRT, RTSP, RTMP, UDP, HLS), NDI and Slideshow (the pictures of a folder)
- Windows: parts of the program as windows of their own, and workspaces that save and restore the arrangement
- Outputs: size, refresh rate and rotation per output; recording with a folder and file name of your choice
- Cues: groups (also random and nested), Take and Playback cues, fades on effect values; tally can be received (TSL, vMix) and shown on controller buttons
- Remote: Blackmagic ATEM switchers, a module for Bitfocus Companion
- The first start opens the test project "Weismehl Demo"
- Much of this is not yet tested on real equipment – please use the Feedback button

- Registration: on the first start the program asks for your name, company and e-mail once – so we know who is testing
- Test versions now run for 60 days after they were built; a yellow tag shows a week before the end, About shows the date
- New inputs: Playlist (films one after another); on Windows also a single window of another program and a web page or YouTube video
- Layers: crop and border per layer; colour tables (LUT) can also be loaded as PNG; the test project can be restored
- Preview quality can be chosen (Eco to Full); the footer shows frame rate and load
- Timing: a screen only sets the pace when its refresh rate matches the project – recordings at 50 fps next to a 60 Hz or 120 Hz screen no longer get doubled frames
- An input that is on air can no longer be removed by mistake
- Windows: the package brings FFmpeg along; helper programs (FFmpeg) now end together with the program
- Much of this is not yet tested on real equipment – please use the Feedback button

- Mac: a web page or a YouTube video can now be an input on the Mac as well (the browser part is downloaded once when you first use it)
- Mac: the package brings FFmpeg along – import, recording, streaming and network inputs work without installing anything
- Web page as an input: the first command after the browser part had restarted was lost (Reload, Play/Pause) – fixed
- Much of this is not yet tested on real equipment – please use the Feedback button

- Import: drag files from the Explorer or Finder into the window – videos that are not HAP are converted by themselves, with a queue, progress and Cancel
- NDI on Windows: the package brings the NDI library along – NDI sources work without installing the NDI Tools (on the Mac the NDI Tools are still needed)
- Crash reports: if the program closed unexpectedly, it asks at the next start whether it may send us a report – only if you agree, and without names of files, inputs, shows or folders
- Log: every session writes a log into the folder "logs" in the media folder; Feedback with technical details includes its last lines and your computer (processor, memory, graphics card, screen sizes)
- Terms of Use: the registration now asks you to accept them; you find them under About and as EULA.html in the package
- T-bar: it no longer jumps at the end of a fade – after a fade by hand the lever rests at its end, and the next fade goes the other way, as on a vision mixer
- New setting Look, Live picture: always in the right window (as before) or alternating (A/B) – after every change the window with the next picture becomes live
- Audio mixer: every bus has a note that is always visible at its channel – for example where the bus goes
- Fixed: after a crash of the picture loop the program could stay in the background on Windows and block a new start
- Much of this is not yet tested on real equipment – please use the Feedback button

- Light: a new Light page – add fixtures from a library of 650 types (Open Fixture Library) or import GDTF files from the manufacturer, arrange them on the stage, select by click or frame, set colour, position, gobo and more in the programmer
- Light: 3D view of the stage – beams, colours, positions and gobos as programmed, from the front, the top or the side; drag to turn
- Light: looks (store, recall with fade, add as a cue) and effects – Chase, Rainbow, Circle and Wave on any group of fixtures
- Light: USB-DMX adapters (Enttec DMX USB Pro, Open DMX) besides Art-Net and sACN
- DMX in: a lighting desk can control the player – a channel fires GO, another moves the T-bar or the master (Settings → Light)
- Picture effects: Hue shift, Pixelate, Mirror, Kaleidoscope, Posterize, RGB shift, Edges and Invert for every input (Picture → Effects → Stylise)
- Outputs: Delay of 0 to 10 frames per output, so a slower projector and an LED wall show in step
- Start with this computer: for installations the player starts by itself, waits, loads a show and fires the first cue (Settings → Project)
- NDI out: send the program as an NDI source
- Webcam: the program as a camera for Zoom, Teams and others (Windows)
- Audio: effects on every bus and the master (EQ, compressor, limiter)
- MultiCorder: record several inputs at the same time
- Much of this is not yet tested on real equipment – please use the Feedback button

- Stress test (new, please join in): Help → Stress test lets the player test itself for 15 minutes to 2 hours and measures how well it runs on your computer. Send us the report with one click. Afterwards your show is back exactly as it was.
- Usage statistics (new, optional): anonymously counts which functions and pages are used and how often – never content or names. Off until you switch it on under Help → About and updates. Show what is sent shows exactly what goes out.
- Menus: a new menu bar with File, Edit, View, Devices and Help. Settings only holds what belongs to your computer; less common footer buttons are under More.
- Shows: open and save like in any other program – with the Windows and macOS dialogs, Open recent, Save as and Ctrl+S. Collect media copies all media next to the show file, so you can take the whole folder to another computer.
- Timeline (new): place clips on tracks, move and trim them, with fades and markers. A timeline plays as one input, starts from a cue and can follow timecode.
- Several computers (first step, experimental): a second player runs along as a node; commands and films stay in sync.
- Audio: every channel strip has a Fade button with its own time – also from a shortcut or trigger.
- Webcam output (Windows): shows program, preview or a single input.
- Outputs: Keep shape stops 16:9 pictures being stretched on portrait screens. Plus a new test pattern.
- Overlays: a channel that is switched off is empty; a new source on a running channel fades in again.
- Cues: cues with a timecode wait for their time, even behind an auto-continue chain.
- Input window: now opens on Position.
- Light: Elgato Key Lights on the Light page, in looks and cues.
- Layers: a film used as a layer starts again every time it goes on air if it is set to Starts from the start.
- Stability: four hours under constant load without a crash. An error in one part no longer stops the player; opening a show no longer freezes the picture.
- Fixed: wide HAP films for LED walls (over 8192 pixels) play directly. Graphics card errors and damaged MOV files no longer close the player. Art-Net timecode keeps running when a lighting desk sends on the network. Very long titles and tickers no longer cost frames. Start with this computer finds the chosen show again. Shows store their media relative to the show file.
- Much of this has not been tested on real equipment yet. Tell us what you notice via Help → Report a bug or ask for a feature.
releases.notes_de:
- Stresstest (neu, bitte mitmachen): Unter Help → Stress test testet sich der Player 15 Minuten bis 2 Stunden selbst und misst, wie gut er auf deinem Rechner läuft. Den Bericht schickst du uns mit einem Klick. Danach ist deine Show wieder genau so da wie vorher.
- Nutzungsstatistik (neu, freiwillig): Zählt anonym, welche Funktionen und Seiten wie oft benutzt werden – nie Inhalte oder Namen. Sie ist aus, bis du sie unter Help → About and updates einschaltest. Show what is sent zeigt genau, was übertragen wird.
- Menüs: Neue Menüleiste mit File, Edit, View, Devices und Help. Settings enthält nur noch, was deinen Rechner betrifft; seltene Knöpfe der Fußleiste liegen unter More.
- Shows: Öffnen und Speichern wie in jedem Programm – mit den Dialogen von Windows und macOS, Open recent, Save as und Strg+S. Collect media kopiert alle Medien neben die Show-Datei; den Ordner nimmst du komplett auf einen anderen Rechner mit.
- Timeline (neu): Clips auf Spuren legen, verschieben und kürzen, mit Fades und Markern. Eine Timeline läuft als ein Input, startet per Cue und kann dem Timecode folgen.
- Mehrere Rechner (erster Schritt, zum Ausprobieren): Ein zweiter Player läuft als Node mit; Befehle und Filme bleiben synchron.
- Audio: Jeder Channel Strip hat einen Fade-Knopf mit eigener Zeit – auch per Taste und Trigger.
- Webcam Output (Windows): zeigt wahlweise Program, Preview oder einen einzelnen Input.
- Outputs: Keep shape verhindert verzerrte 16:9-Bilder auf hochkant gestellten Bildschirmen. Dazu ein neues Testbild.
- Overlays: Ein ausgeschalteter Kanal ist leer; eine neue Quelle auf einem laufenden Kanal wird neu eingeblendet.
- Cues: Cues mit Timecode warten auf ihre Zeit, auch hinter einer Auto-continue-Kette.
- Input-Fenster: öffnet jetzt mit Position.
- Licht: Elgato Key Lights auf der Seite Light, in Looks und Cues.
- Layer: Ein Film als Layer startet bei jedem Auftritt neu, wenn er auf Starts from the start steht.
- Stabilität: Vier Stunden Dauerlast ohne Absturz. Ein Fehler in einem Teil hält den Player nicht mehr an; beim Öffnen einer Show steht das Bild nicht mehr.
- Behoben: Breite HAP-Filme für LED-Wände (über 8192 Pixel) laufen direkt. Fehler der Grafikkarte und beschädigte MOV-Dateien beenden den Player nicht mehr. Art-Net-Timecode läuft weiter, wenn ein Lichtpult im Netz sendet. Sehr lange Titel und Ticker kosten keine Bilder mehr. Start with this computer findet die gewählte Show wieder. Shows speichern ihre Medien relativ zur Show-Datei.
- Vieles davon ist noch nicht an echter Technik geprüft. Schreib uns über Help → Report a bug or ask for a feature, was dir auffällt.

releases.notes:
- PowerPoint as an input (new, Windows with PowerPoint installed): Add input → PowerPoint. Animations, transitions and videos look exactly like in PowerPoint. Prev and Next on the tile show the slide, e.g. 3 / 12.
- Presenter (new): in the input window under Video, switch on Presenter – a wireless clicker (MasterCue, PerfectCue, Logitech …) then steps the presentation, even when another window is in front. Right arrow / Page down: next, Left arrow / Page up: back, B: black screen.
- Several computers: Devices → Nodes shows every player on the network – join with one click, the media are copied to the node by themselves. The Outputs page is now called Stage; each output has a Computer field.
- Performance in the footer now shows the render time: average and longest picture of the last second, e.g. 2.0 ms · max 11 ms.
- Timeline: the view keeps its zoom when you switch between timelines.
- Mac: Syphon output sends program to Resolume, MadMapper, OBS and others on the same Mac.
- Licence: Help → About has a field for a licence code. The beta keeps running without one.
- Limits: up to 64 slices per show and 2,000 cues per cue list.
- Stability: very long frames and slow commands are written to the session log, so a report shows what happened.
- The manual is now also in English.
- Coming next week: the Windows packages will be signed by Microsoft, very likely the Mac packages by Apple too – no more warnings on first start, and the webcam output finally works on the Mac.
- Much of this has not been tested on real equipment yet. Tell us what you notice via Help → Report a bug or ask for a feature.
releases.notes_de:
- PowerPoint als Input (neu, Windows mit installiertem PowerPoint): Add input → PowerPoint. Animationen, Übergänge und Videos sehen aus wie in PowerPoint. Prev und Next auf der Kachel, dazu die Folie, z. B. 3 / 12.
- Presenter (neu): Im Input-Fenster unter Video schaltest du Presenter ein – dann steuert ein Funk-Presenter (MasterCue, PerfectCue, Logitech …) die Präsentation, auch wenn ein anderes Fenster vorne ist. Pfeil rechts / Bild ab: weiter, Pfeil links / Bild auf: zurück, B: Schwarzbild.
- Mehrere Rechner: Devices → Nodes zeigt jeden Player im Netz – mit einem Klick verbinden, die Medien kopiert der Player selbst auf den Node. Die Seite Outputs heißt jetzt Stage; jeder Output hat ein Feld Computer.
- Die Leistungsanzeige in der Fußleiste zeigt jetzt die Renderzeit: Mittel und längstes Bild der letzten Sekunde, z. B. 2.0 ms · max 11 ms.
- Timeline: Die Ansicht behält ihren Zoom, wenn du zwischen Timelines wechselst.
- Mac: Der Syphon-Output schickt Program an Resolume, MadMapper, OBS und andere auf demselben Mac.
- Lizenz: Unter Help → About gibt es ein Feld für einen Lizenz-Code. Die Beta läuft weiter ohne.
- Grenzen: bis zu 64 Slices je Show und 2.000 Cues je Cue-Liste.
- Stabilität: Sehr lange Bilder und langsame Befehle stehen im Protokoll der Sitzung – eine Meldung zeigt dann, was passiert ist.
- Das Handbuch gibt es jetzt auch auf Englisch.
- Ab kommender Woche: Die Windows-Pakete sind dann von Microsoft signiert, die Mac-Pakete höchstwahrscheinlich auch von Apple – keine Warnungen mehr beim ersten Start, und der Webcam Output läuft endlich auch auf dem Mac.
- Vieles davon ist noch nicht an echter Technik geprüft. Schreib uns über Help → Report a bug or ask for a feature, was dir auffällt.

releases.notes:
- Text titles (new): Add input → Title → style "Text (free)". Kicker, headline over several lines (| starts a new line, *word* turns orange), subline; position, size, alignment and your own font (put the .ttf files into the folder fonts in the media folder, e.g. Montserrat). Change everything in the title window – it shows at once, even on air.
- Title animations (new): fade in, rise line by line, word by word, slide in from the left, typewriter – with duration and delay. They start when the title goes on air.
- Upright 9:16 (new): Settings → Recording → "Set up 9:16". One take, two files: the normal recording and an upright 1080 × 1920 file for Reels, TikTok and Shorts. "Section" chooses which part of the picture it shows.
- Recordings now have their exact size – for example exactly 1080 × 1920 when upright.
- Stage: the picture always fits the window, also upright canvases and portrait screens. Zoom with the mouse wheel or − / Fit / +.
- Much of this has not been tested on real equipment yet. Tell us what you notice via Help → Report a bug or ask for a feature.
releases.notes_de:
- Text-Titel (neu): Add input → Title → Form „Text (free)“. Kopfzeile, Überschrift über mehrere Zeilen (| beginnt eine neue Zeile, *Wort* wird orange), Unterzeile; Lage, Größe, Ausrichtung und deine eigene Schrift (die .ttf-Dateien in den Ordner fonts im Medienordner legen, z. B. Montserrat). Alles änderst du im Titel-Fenster – sofort im Bild, auch auf Sendung.
- Animationen für Titel (neu): Einblenden, Zeile für Zeile aufsteigen, Wort für Wort, von links hineinschieben, Schreibmaschine – mit Dauer und Verzögerung. Sie starten, sobald der Titel auf Sendung geht.
- Hochformat 9:16 (neu): Settings → Recording → „Set up 9:16“. Ein Take, zwei Dateien: die normale Aufnahme und eine hochkante in 1080 × 1920 für Reels, TikTok und Shorts. Mit „Section“ wählst du den Ausschnitt.
- Aufnahmen haben jetzt ihre genaue Größe – hochkant zum Beispiel genau 1080 × 1920.
- Stage: Das Bild passt immer ins Fenster, auch bei hochkanten Canvases und Hochkant-Bildschirmen. Zoomen mit dem Mausrad oder − / Fit / +.
- Vieles davon ist noch nicht an echter Technik geprüft. Schreib uns über Help → Report a bug or ask for a feature, was dir auffällt.
